newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cautious on North Korea peace talks report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cautious on North Korea peace talks report.

text.p: U.S. officials reacted cautiously on Tuesday to reports that North Korea has agreed to a meeting of senior South Korean, U.S. and Chinese officials to arrange four-way peace tlaks.
"There is nothing I know of that is imminent," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns who is in San Franciso with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright enroute to Asia.
Another U.S. official said there could be announcement in a few days but he was unaware anything was planned for Wednesday, as reported from South Korea.

A Seoul government source said on Wednesday "Pyongyang has accepted a suggestion that senior oficials from the two Koreas, the United States and China meet around early August to set an agenda and other details for the peace tallks."
The four-nation talks, proposed by the United States and South Korea last year, aim to work out a peace settlement to replace a fraying armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
Seoul's foreign ministry spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung declined to confirm the North Korean agreement but said: "There will be announcement on four way peacetalks at 10:00 p.m. (1300 GMT) today."
Famine-threatened North Korea in April agreed in principle to join the peace talks but tied participation to largescale food aid and an easing of U.S. trade sanctions.
South Korea and the United States have said such assistance could be discussed during peace talks.
On June 18, U.S. and Korean negotiators discussed the peace talks proposal in New York as U.S. officials voiced new optimism that Pyongyang was near agreement on negotiations.

At that time, U.S. officials told Reuter three-side talks were "fine tuning" an announcement that would commit North Korea to attending a senior-level meeting that would set an agenda and other details for the peace talks.
